caption: The drawing is presented on a beige-colored sheet with visible signs of age on the left margin. It contains two primary orthographic projections of an object labeled as "Settle Table" from the Brooklyn Museum, as indicated in a boxed label at the bottom left. The left half of the drawing is labeled “FRONT VIEW” and depicts the object as a rectangular structure with a backrest and armrests, with measurements in inches annotated in red dotted lines and numbers. The seat width is marked as 35 inches, and the full width as 32.5 inches, with armrest thicknesses of 7/8 inches on each side; the height is marked as 17.25 inches. The right half is labeled “SIDE VIEW” and shows the profile of the same object, revealing a tall backrest with a rounded top, a curved armrest, and structural details such as a bracing element under the seat. The full height from base to top is 30.5 inches, with additional measurements for various components, including a large semicircular cut-out at the base. All lines are drawn in black ink, with red ink used for dimension lines and measurements. At the bottom right, the name "B. Holst-Grubbe" is lightly inscribed. A scale in inches appears centrally at the bottom of the page.
title: Settle-table
